newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tribal rebels want Bangladesh peace talks delayed.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels want Bangladesh peace talks delayed.

text.p: Tribal rebels fighting for self-rule in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts have asked the government to postpone peace talks from April 30 to May 11, officials said on Tuesday.

The request came from the Parbatya Chattagram Janasanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the Shanti Bahini guerrilla group, said Ushatan Talukder, convenor of the Liason Committee in the Hill Tracts.
"The PCJSS in its letter to Talukder did not give any specific reason for the proposed shift," one government official told reporters.
Talukder said the PCJSS mentioned "unavoidable circumstances" and requested the talks be delayed from April 30 to May 11.
The rebels have held two rounds of peace talks in Dhaka since Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took office in June 1996 and pledged to find a political solution to the Hill Tracts problems.
The last round was held on February 25.
Shati Bahini, comprising Chakma tribesmen, began the insurgency in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected its demand for autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Trtacts bordering India and Burma.
It also wants some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the hill and forest region
The government has turned down that demand, but it has been trying to reclaim tribal lands which have been occupied by the settlers and return them to tribepeople being repatriated from India.
Of some 50,000 tribespeople who fled across the boder over a decade or so, more than 6,000 were repatriated between March 28 and April 7 following an agreement between Dhaka and New Delhi.
The next phase of repatriation was expected to begin in May if the Shanti Bahini and refugee leaders had found rehabilitation of the returnees satisfactory, officials said..
Over 8,500 civilians, securitymen and rebels have been killed in the insurgency, according to official figures.
